ports.name: Extension porter (pig-porter, pig-extension-porter)
ports.summary: The strict porting Skill, the equivalence harness (pigeq) and the two Piglets that carry them. This is the workflow every other row is ported with.
ports.credit: The pigpen-pi-extension-port Skill adapts the PiG Porter procedure and TypeScript-to-Go porting rules from PiG, https://github.com/MichaelKinsy/PiG, by Michael Kinsy (MIT), at commit d86eb93f217e64b655e9ee6f48c93a9afd107697.
ports.notes: Reviewed (ACCEPT-WITH-FIXES). Lane pigpen-porter-driver keeps tuning the Skill and harness from every port below. Reviewed and merged for the first release.

ports.name: dirty-repo-guard
ports.summary: Pi example extension that refuses a session switch or fork while the git tree is dirty. The first port made with the porter.
ports.credit: Go port of the dirty-repo-guard.ts example of Pi, https://github.com/earendil-works/pi, by Mario Zechner (MIT, v0.87.1, commit f07218c4d4bbc12bef056a7058c3dd49dfe41abe).
ports.notes: 11/11 scenarios identical to Pi, 17/17 mutations killed.

ports.name: herdr agent-state reporter
ports.summary: Reports PiG idle, working and blocked to herdr through its documented pane report-agent contract.
ports.credit: Original work by Michael Kinsy (MIT). Implements herdr's documented agent-state contract; no herdr code is copied.
ports.notes: Go port on the public SDK (it replaced the earlier Node extension). Reviewed and merged for the first release.

ports.name: Web search and fetch (pi-web-access)
ports.summary: Search, fetch, retain sources and retrieve bounded content: providers, routing, cache, extraction. Delivered in reviewed slices.
ports.credit: Go port of pi-web-access 0.33.0, https://github.com/nicobailon/pi-web-access, by Nico Bailon (MIT), at commit 9a734ed195da2f4cccc2fb5e7128f6774a380f47.
ports.notes: npm 483,117 in 30 days, 1,562 stars (2026-09-29). No browser-cookie access by default; no paid fallback without configuration. Reviewed and merged for the first release.

ports.name: ACP: editors drive a PiG agent (pi-acp)
ports.summary: stdio Agent Client Protocol adapter over the PiG agent, with declared capability limits. A standalone bridge, not an extension.
ports.credit: Go port of pi-acp 0.0.34, https://github.com/svkozak/pi-acp, by Sergii Kozak (MIT), at commit b0581c9c1d675e634234674484247008b03d69b4. The protocol schema is from Agent Client Protocol, https://github.com/agentclientprotocol/typescript-sdk, by Zed Industries (Apache-2.0), commit 73bc30649b650de320340c782733bf69a545bd28.
ports.notes: npm 300,748 in 30 days. Port from the ACP spec, not from pi-acp's unmerged pull requests. Reviewed and merged for the first release.

ports.name: AHP: multi-client session host (pi-ahp)
ports.summary: Host extension serving Microsoft's Agent Host Protocol over WebSocket: reconnect, reconciliation, auth. No listener unless configured.
ports.credit: Go port of pi-ahp, https://github.com/Qusic/pi-ahp, by Bang Lee (Qusic) (MIT), at commit 4065e98309b03c1d2d916300856c3c21a9c10674. The protocol types and reducers are from Agent Host Protocol, https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol, by Microsoft Corporation (MIT), commit 296b25e7b698a4a84a0ee5a28d9573e70048a0bf.
ports.notes: Lowest demand of the protocol rows (1,206 npm downloads in 30 days); the protocol is Microsoft's and VS Code uses it. Reviewed and merged for the first release.

ports.name: A2A: serve PiG tasks, call remote agents
ports.summary: Original adapter on a2a-go: an A2A server for PiG tasks and a client for remote agents, interoperating with kagent. Listener off unless configured.
ports.credit: Original adapter built on a2a-go v2.6.0, https://github.com/a2aproject/a2a-go, by The A2A Authors, Linux Foundation (Apache-2.0), commit ebf17c56ef7e63c72883a45454a538bbc0df66b8.
ports.notes: No popular Pi A2A extension exists; @bacnh85/pi-a2a is a behaviour reference only. Reviewed and merged for the first release.

ports.name: Jev: typed judgments and gates (y0usaf/pi-jev)
ports.summary: Tool-call gate, output judge and jev_ask, with the roadmap's defect corrections. Opt-in; discloses that content leaves the machine.
ports.credit: Go port of pi-jev, https://github.com/y0usaf/pi-jev, by y0usaf (MIT), at commit 88e5fb3888948e7065110d47cdf6ac57abb71ba4.
ports.notes: Owner-approved foundation. Small ecosystem (605 npm downloads in 30 days); pi-warden and pi-typesafe are the more installed Jev packages. Reviewed and merged for the first release.

ports.name: TypeSafe client (typesafe-sdk-js, system-one-adapter-python)
ports.summary: Shared Go client for the TypeSafe API, plus a backend that answers the same typed questions with the model PiG is configured with. Used by jev, pi-typesafe and pi-warden.
ports.credit: Go port of the TypeSafe SDK (typesafe-sdk-js, https://github.com/typesafe-ai/typesafe-sdk-js, v0.6.0) and of system-one-adapter-python, https://github.com/typesafe-ai/system-one-adapter-python (v0.2.1), both by TypeSafe AI (MIT). Cross-checks use WorkflowEvals, https://github.com/typesafe-ai/WorkflowEvals, by TypeSafe AI (Apache-2.0), commit 0ac3b8ad845429f0d8e064ecfb2430a47c5a25cb.
ports.notes: Tests use a fake TypeSafe server; no real API call without an owner-supplied TYPESAFE_API_KEY. The Go contract is committed first so the three extension lanes can build against it. Reviewed and merged for the first release.

ports.name: pi-typesafe (DevMortimer)
ports.summary: The batched typesafe_evaluate tool and the typed API for extension authors, on the shared Go client. Off by default.
ports.credit: Go port of pi-typesafe 0.8.0, https://github.com/DevMortimer/pi-typesafe, by Ryan Gapac (DevMortimer) (MIT), at commit ed439f834665ad6fc652787f5ba7c23852566d49.
ports.notes: npm 7,453 in 30 days (2026-09-29). Depends on the typesafe-client row. Discloses that content goes to the TypeSafe API unless the own-model backend is selected. Reviewed and merged for the first release.

ports.name: pi-warden (DevMortimer)
ports.summary: Guardrails that steer instead of interrupt: irreversible calls, off-task calls, stuck loops, unverified done claims. Opt-in, on the shared Go client.
ports.credit: Go port of pi-warden 0.74.1, https://github.com/DevMortimer/pi-warden, by Ryan Gapac (DevMortimer) (MIT), at commit a12b2703b2c7ac32401fe13f4ce037d673a5f113. It also uses pi-typesafe, https://github.com/DevMortimer/pi-typesafe, by Ryan Gapac (DevMortimer) (MIT), at commit ed439f834665ad6fc652787f5ba7c23852566d49, through the shared TypeSafe client.
ports.notes: npm 7,030 in 30 days, 154 stars (2026-09-29). Depends on the typesafe-client row. A launch-video demo feature; the own-model backend must work. Re-pinned at the warden merge from 0f11867 (the listing-time head) to a12b2703, the commit the port was made against (components/warden/provenance.json); the pi-typesafe upstream is its second one. Reviewed and merged for the first release.

ports.name: pig-play: shared pig sprite and terminal game library
ports.summary: The canonical pixel pig, palette, half-block rasteriser and terminal game plumbing that every pig game builds on.
ports.credit: Sprite, pixel rasteriser, arcade scenery and terminal game plumbing moved from PiG, https://github.com/MichaelKinsy/PiG, by Michael Kinsy (MIT), at commit d86eb93f217e64b655e9ee6f48c93a9afd107697.
ports.notes: Reviewed and merged for the first release.

ports.name: PiG Runner
ports.summary: Obstacle runner starring the pig; starts only on an explicit command.
ports.credit: The pigrunner extension moved from PiG, https://github.com/MichaelKinsy/PiG, by Michael Kinsy (MIT), at commit d86eb93f217e64b655e9ee6f48c93a9afd107697.
ports.notes: Reviewed and merged for the first release.

ports.name: Angry Pigs
ports.summary: Pig slingshot puzzle game; starts only on an explicit command.
ports.credit: The angrypigs extension moved from PiG, https://github.com/MichaelKinsy/PiG, by Michael Kinsy (MIT), at commit d86eb93f217e64b655e9ee6f48c93a9afd107697.
ports.notes: Reviewed and merged for the first release.

ports.name: Pig Snake
ports.summary: New snake game where every apple adds another pig head, so a herd forms behind the leader. Explicit command only.
ports.credit: Original game by Michael Kinsy (MIT). The pig sprite art is from PiG, https://github.com/MichaelKinsy/PiG, by Michael Kinsy (MIT), commit d86eb93f217e64b655e9ee6f48c93a9afd107697.
ports.notes: Sprite access sits behind one interface so it can switch to the shared pig-play library. Reviewed and merged for the first release.

ports.name: session-ingest (read_session)
ports.summary: Read another PiG session: turn, tools and stats modes. Moved from the owner's own extensions to the public PiG Go SDK.
ports.credit: Original work by Michael Kinsy (MIT), moved from the owner's own extensions.
ports.notes: No popular equivalent exists. Reviewed and merged for the first release.

ports.name: context-info (/context, /tools, /cost, /prompts)
ports.summary: Context, tools, cost and prompt inspection commands with an opt-in footer widget. Moved from the owner's own extensions to the public PiG Go SDK.
ports.credit: Original work by Michael Kinsy (MIT), moved from the owner's own extensions.
ports.notes: Moved unless a far more popular Pi extension covers the same job; the lane reports if one does. Reviewed and merged for the first release.

ports.name: General development Skills (dev-skills)
ports.summary: Eight general development Skills (tdd, diagnosing-bugs, handoff, research, grilling, prototype, code-review, commit) adapted from public Skills, as one Skills Package. Not in batteries.
ports.credit: Skills adapted from mattpocock/skills, https://github.com/mattpocock/skills, by Matt Pocock (MIT), at commit d81f3a183412e71a5b1e84ca21bc1a35eea03a60, and from mitsuhiko/agent-stuff, https://github.com/mitsuhiko/agent-stuff, by Armin Ronacher (Apache-2.0), at commit 0865c849befd2021490679f96a8dee58c84ac857. Adaptation by Michael Kinsy (MIT).
ports.notes: Names take the pigpen- prefix the Skill gate requires. The adaptations were made from an earlier upstream revision whose commit was not recorded (see the Package CREDITS.md). Reviewed and merged for the first release.

ports.name: rpiv-todo
ports.summary: Model-facing todo list shown as a live overlay that survives reload and compaction.
ports.credit: Go port of @juicesharp/rpiv-todo 2.11.0 from rpiv-mono, https://github.com/juicesharp/rpiv-mono, by juicesharp (MIT), at commit 61904e69e1a50e12585bdf15f0310e633a62ba36.
ports.notes: npm 200,994 in 30 days. Size S, 3-5 days. The overlay is widget lines (Go SDK stand-in).

ports.name: rpiv-ask-user-question
ports.summary: Structured multi-question questionnaire the model calls instead of guessing, with an RPC fallback and locales.
ports.credit: Go port of @juicesharp/rpiv-ask-user-question 2.11.0 from rpiv-mono, https://github.com/juicesharp/rpiv-mono, by juicesharp (MIT), at commit 61904e69e1a50e12585bdf15f0310e633a62ba36.
ports.notes: npm 274,750 in 30 days. Size M, 6-10 days. The owner's Go ask extension is the base. Known gap: pi.events (named skipped tests).

ports.name: Plannotator
ports.summary: Plan mode with a browser review UI, code and PR diff review, and annotate-last-message. The flagship demo.
ports.credit: Go port of @plannotator/pi-extension 0.27.22 from plannotator, https://github.com/backnotprop/plannotator, by backnotprop (MIT OR Apache-2.0), at commit 3c9d79b36dbfbfcb7a180a52a9b7c60fc7d315df.
ports.notes: npm 105,444 in 30 days, 9,065 stars (cross-agent). Size L, 15-25 days: net/http plus the embedded prebuilt UI bundle, not a rewrite of the React UI. Start early; version 0.27 churns, so keep the pin.

ports.name: Ponytail
ports.summary: The "lazy senior dev" mode: /ponytail modes, review, audit, gain and debt commands, plus six skills.
ports.credit: Go port of @dietrichgebert/ponytail 4.10.0, https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail, by Dietrich Gebert (MIT), at commit 1d95ff7d39de12d87014ea40d4e22201bddc501b.
ports.notes: npm 69,188 in 30 days, 148,287 stars (marketing signal). Size XS, 1-3 days. Do not repeat the author's own 54% claim as ours.

ports.name: Langfuse observability
ports.summary: Traces prompts, turns, generations and tool calls to Langfuse. Opt-in; prompts leave the machine.
ports.credit: Go port of @langfuse/pi-observability-plugin 0.1.2, https://github.com/langfuse/pi-observability-plugin, by Langfuse GmbH (MIT), at commit 801108fac709ee5e72aa57b5a03ab4bfb1d2195b.
ports.notes: npm 249,668 in 30 days but 11 stars: the count looks partly automated. Size S, 4-7 days. Pairs with LangSmith (@langchain/langsmith-pi-extension) as one observability battery. No default telemetry in batteries.

ports.name: pi-subagents (Nico Bailon)
ports.summary: Delegation to child sessions: single, parallel, chains, fleet and status views, council mode, worktree isolation.
ports.credit: Go port of pi-subagents 0.73.1, https://github.com/nicobailon/pi-subagents, by Nico Bailon (MIT), at commit 8a403efba6975988cc0488ec8bb941db5ef1a19e.
ports.notes: Deferred to its own long lane (size XL, 25-45 days). npm 506,599 in 30 days. Needs an owner decision on the JavaScript workflow runtime (no Node dependency is approved). The owner's Go subagent is the base.
